description: We are Hers & Hertz, educators passionate about science, creativity, and inclusive learning. Our strengths are teaching, storytelling, and communication. Through EarthSonic, we aim to turn NASA Earth visualisations into sound, helping people hear change and feel connected to our planet.
summary:
Listen to the Planet. Discover the Unseen.

What if we could hear our planet changing—not just see it?

Earth's environmental changes are monitored through vast scientific datasets, yet much of this information is presented visually, creating accessibility barriers for blind and low-vision audiences and limiting alternative ways to explore complex environmental patterns.

EarthSonic is an intelligent, multisensory sonification platform that transforms NASA GISS data into interactive soundscapes. Our framework translates environmental variables such as pollutant concentrations, temporal changes and spatial patterns into musical elements including pitch, rhythm and timbre.

Using NASA's GISS surface temperature, users can listen to atmospheric changes, explore environmental patterns and compare data across time and regions. Combining synchronised visualisations, interactive audio and accessibility features such as spoken explanations and screen-reader support, EarthSonic makes Earth science more inclusive and engaging.

More than seeing our planet change, it's about hearing its story.
details:
EarthSonic: Listen to Our Living Planet

Tagline: See It. Hear It. Understand It.

EarthSonic is an interactive Earth Information Jukebox that transforms NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies (GISS) Surface Temperature visualisations into dynamic musical soundscapes. Our project explores a creative way to experience and understand geographical temperature variations by translating visual information into sound.

What does it do and how does it work?

EarthSonic allows users to select an Earth science story, view its NASA GISS visualisation and listen as its geographical patterns are transformed into sound. Our initial experience, The Pulse of Our Planet: Surface Temperature, uses NASA's GISS Surface Temperature visualisation to explore the spatial distribution and variations of Earth's surface temperatures.

The application analyses visual characteristics such as colour intensity, pixel distribution, geographical patterns and temperature variations across the visualisation. These characteristics are translated into musical elements: higher temperature intensity influences higher pitches, lower temperature intensity produces lower pitches, colour intensity influences volume, spatial distribution determines note density, and variations across the visualisation influence rhythm and tempo.

The application generates sounds dynamically and synchronises them with the displayed GISS visualisation. Rather than simply playing a pre-recorded soundtrack, EarthSonic creates an interactive audio experience derived from the visual characteristics of the scientific information.

Benefits and intended impact

EarthSonic offers an alternative and engaging way to explore geographical and environmental information through both sight and sound. It aims to make complex surface temperature patterns more accessible and understandable, particularly for students, educators, the general public and people with visual impairments.

For education, it introduces an innovative approach to teaching Geography, Earth Science and environmental studies through multisensory learning. For accessibility, it provides an additional way to experience scientific visualisations beyond conventional visual displays. For environmental awareness, it transforms geographical temperature information into an interactive experience that can inspire curiosity, understanding and appreciation of our changing planet.

Tools and technologies

Our development uses:

  • NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis visualisation as the primary scientific visual source.
  • Google Antigravity to build the web interface.
  • Canva to develop the visual identity, interface concepts and presentation materials.
  • AI-assisted coding tools to support code generation, technical problem-solving and development.

Creativity and Innovation

The creativity of EarthSonic lies in connecting GISS, Earth science and sound through interactive technology. We are exploring how geographical temperature information can become an experience that people do not just see, but hear.

Each surface temperature visualisation becomes a unique soundscape shaped by its geographical and visual characteristics. Warmer and cooler areas are represented through different pitches, while spatial distributions and variations influence musical patterns. This creates opportunities to explore environmental themes through distinctive auditory experiences.

By transforming conventional GISS visualisations into interactive soundscapes, EarthSonic introduces an alternative approach to scientific communication and inclusive environmental learning.

Factors considered during development

Our team considers scientific accuracy, meaningful data-to-sound relationships, accessibility, ease of use and technical feasibility. We aim to ensure that the generated sounds correspond to identifiable characteristics of NASA's GISS visualisations, with clear explanations of what each sound represents. We also consider the needs of users with different levels of scientific knowledge and visual ability, as well as browser compatibility, audio performance and the limitations of our development resources.

Through EarthSonic, we hope to demonstrate that science can be experienced in more than one way. By transforming NASA GISS surface temperature visualisations into sound, we invite everyone to discover a new perspective on our living planet.

EarthSonic — See It. Hear It. Understand It.
